title: Reliable onboard LiDAR-inertial localization
description: Physical signal and geometric quality cues help LiDAR-inertial odometry decide how strongly each observation should influence the motion estimate.
introduction: A robot needs more than a stream of measurements: it needs to know which measurements to trust. This work weights LiDAR observations before they correct the inertial estimate, improving localization in environments with uneven sensing quality.

problem.heading: Every return is not equally informative.
paragraphs: A rigid surface can provide stable geometric constraints, while vegetation, distant returns and weakly structured regions offer less reliable corrections. Treating these observations alike can let poor measurements distort the state estimate.

LiDAR-inertial odometry combines fast motion prediction from an IMU with geometric correction from a laser scanner. The challenge is to assess measurement reliability before an observation contributes to that correction.

approach.heading: Assess trust before updating the state.
paragraphs: The method introduces proactive measurement weighting into FAST-LIO2. It examines local intensity consistency, geometric planarity and measurement range to estimate how much confidence to place in each LiDAR point.
These physical and geometric cues adjust measurement covariance. More reliable observations exert greater influence on the state correction, while weaker observations contribute less.

The reliability study builds on the group's broader onboard localization work. Its benchmark comparison is distinct from the general mapping demonstration shown here, which comes from John Lewis Devassy's exploration experiments.

steps.text: Evaluate intensity consistency, surface planarity and range reliability.

steps.text: Adjust observation covariance before the LiDAR state update.

evidence.label: Featureless benchmark evaluation
evidence.text: The published quantitative reliability evaluation uses the MARS-LVIG Featureless benchmark. It evaluates the weighted FAST-LIO2 correction separately from the outdoor mapping examples.

evidence.label: Qualitative outdoor reconstruction
evidence.text: The golf-course reconstructions provide qualitative evidence of geometric consistency. They should be read as outdoor mapping examples, rather than as the source of the benchmark's percentage error reduction.

evidence.label: General onboard mapping demonstration
evidence.text: The real-flight clip from John Lewis Devassy's work illustrates the underlying LiDAR–IMU localization layer and online map registration. It is not a direct comparison of the reliability-weighted method with its baseline.
